transcript: respected dignitaries, esteemed faculty, and my dear friends. Today, as the tri-colour rises majestically above us, we stand together to commemorate the 80th year of India's independence. Seventy-nine years since the nation broke the shuttles of colonialism and began writing its own destiny. But independence was now merely the freedom to govern ourselves. It was the freedom to dream without limits, to question without fear and to build without permission. Our freedom fighters surrendered their youths at comfort as in countless cases their very lives. Not for the India of one generation, but for the India of generations yet unborn. and today we are those generations. The battlefield has changed, the challenges have evolved yet the responsibility remains unchanged. Our soldiers guard our borders, our farmers sustain our civilization, our scientists expand the frontiers of possibility, our innovators are shaping tomorrow and we the youth of India are the custodians of what India becomes next. In an age of artificial intelligence, technological revolutions and global transformation, India cannot afford to merely follow the future. We must have the courage to create it because the greatness of a nation is not measured merely by its economy, its skyscrapers or its technological prowess. It is measured by the character of its citizens by how honestly we live, how courageously we speak, how compassionately we treat one another and how responsibly we use the freedom we inherited. So on this Indian theory of independence, let us not merely ask what has India given us. Let us ask what are we giving India. Let us choose integrity when dishonesty is convenient. Let us choose unity when division is easier. Let us choose courage when silence is comfortable. Because the freedom of 1947 was their gift to us. The India of tomorrow must be our gift to them. And when the generations after us look back at this moment, let them not say that we merely inherited a free India. Let them say that we had the courage to build a greater one. Let the triangle not merely fly above us today, let its courage live within us every single day. Jai Hind, Jai Bharat.
